dedupe_keys.name: argoverse 1 and 2 autonomous driving sensor lidar and motion forecasting datasets with hd maps of six us cities

description: Argoverse is a family of public autonomous driving datasets distinguished by detailed high-definition (HD) maps of lane geometry and drivable area. It was created by Argo AI with faculty and students from Carnegie Mellon University and the Georgia Institute of Technology; after Argo AI closed, the Argoverse team continues to support the datasets, APIs, leaderboards and competitions. Coverage: six US cities (Austin, Detroit, Miami, Pittsburgh, Palo Alto and Washington, D.C.). Argoverse 2 contains four datasets: a sensor dataset of 1,000 annotated 3D scenarios with lidar, stereo and ring camera imagery; a motion forecasting dataset of 250,000 scenarios with trajectories of many object types; a lidar dataset of 20,000 unannotated sequences; and a map change dataset of 1,000 scenarios, 200 with real HD map changes. Argoverse 1 offered 3D tracking, stereo and motion forecasting data. Format and access: downloads with a common Python API for loading data and maps; free. Licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, non-commercial use only. Caveats: the data cover selected neighbourhoods of the operator's test areas, are tuned to perception research, and the HD maps are not an authoritative road inventory. Simulation uses: trajectory and road geometry inputs for agent-based traffic and vehicle behaviour models, and HD map examples for road digital twins. Related records: the Waymo Open Dataset (data-waymo-open-dataset) and nuScenes (data-nuscenes-autonomous-driving-dataset) are comparable driving datasets.
